## 🔒 Fixes

- **Fixed: on some phones, reopening Pocket Sense after closing it could lose the encryption key**, and the app said it couldn't open your data. Reported on a RedMagic 8S Pro (Android 13). The most likely cause: by default, the secure-storage library deletes everything it holds when Android's Keystore gives it an error at startup. That's now turned off: if the Keystore misbehaves, you get an error with **Try again**, and nothing is deleted. Data already lost this way can't be recovered, so keep automatic backups on (**Settings → Backup**).
- **With a PIN set, the app now stays locked if the Keystore can't be read.** Before, an error there opened the app without asking for the PIN.
- On Android, the error now names Android's keystore instead of the Linux keyring.

## Download
**Android**
- Also on **[F-Droid](https://f-droid.org/packages/ace.software.pocketsense/)**, which keeps it updated. It ships these same signed APKs, so you can switch between the two and keep your data.
- **`PocketSense-v2.2.8-arm64-v8a.apk`**: almost all modern Android phones. Use this one if unsure.
- `PocketSense-v2.2.8-armeabi-v7a.apk`: older 32-bit phones
- `PocketSense-v2.2.8-x86_64.apk`: emulators and Chromebooks

Installs as an update over any earlier version and keeps your data.

**Linux (x86_64)**: pick one.
- **Debian, Ubuntu, Mint:** `PocketSense-v2.2.8-linux-x64.deb`
  ```sh
  sudo apt install ./PocketSense-v2.2.8-linux-x64.deb
  ```
- **Fedora, openSUSE:** `PocketSense-v2.2.8-linux-x64.rpm`
  ```sh
  sudo dnf install ./PocketSense-v2.2.8-linux-x64.rpm   # or: sudo zypper install
  ```
- **Any distro:** `PocketSense-v2.2.8-linux-x64.AppImage`. Make it executable and run it.
- **Any distro:** `PocketSense-v2.2.8-linux-x64.tar.gz`. Unpack it and run `./PocketSense/pocket_sense`.

All need glibc 2.35 or newer and a running keyring (GNOME Keyring or KWallet). With the AppImage or the tarball you also need GTK 3, and `parecord` for voice entry (`pulseaudio-utils` on Debian/Ubuntu/Fedora, `libpulse` on Arch).
